newsitem.title: CHINA: PRESS DIGEST - Chinese newspapers - April 17.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Chinese newspapers - April 17.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Chinese political and business stories in leading newspapers, prepared by Reuters in Beijing. Reuters has not checked the stories and does not guarantee their accuracy. Telephone: (8610) 6532-1921. Fax: (8610) 6532-4978.
PEOPLE'S DAILY
- Communist Party reaffirms commitment to building a clean and honest government by banning senior officials from engaging in personal profit-seeking and other activities
- Li Ruihuan urges provinces and regions to continue to provide economic assistance to Tibet, says this is important directly related to struggle against the Dalai Lama's splittist activities
XINHUA DAILY TELEGRAPH
- Foreign Ministry spokesman Shen Guofang urges United States to promptly correct wrongful decision to provide Taiwan with F-16 fighter jets.
- Chinese President Jiang Zemin meets president of Congress of Peru Victor Joyway Rojas as "old friend" of Chinese people
- Another strong earthquake with magnitude of 6.3 on Richter scale hits Jiashi in northwestern Xinjiang
FINANCIAL NEWS
- PICC chairman says to continue investigating serious economic cases, corruption
- Central bank sets up its own Communist Party school
- China sets May interest rate subsidy at zero percent
CHINA BUSINESS TIMES
- China seen likely to adjust interest rate slightly if current macro-economic situation continues
ECONOMIC DAILY
- Mobile telephone users in Beijing expected to hit 500,000 by end-1997
- China diesel oil shortfall seen at 2.3 million tonnes in first quarter, prices seen holding at relatively high levels
FINANCIAL MORNING POST
- PICC Property pays $6.25 million in compensation to Shenzhen Marine Transport Co Ltd
ECONOMIC INFORMATION DAILY
- China flower and plant industry gross output value hits 4.8 billion in 1996
CHINA DAILY
- China is planning to standardise its growing securities market by learning from international experience, says Zhou Zhengqing, chairman of Securities Committee under State Council
